title: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — Employment Situation News Release, July 2024 (2 August 2024 vintage)
use: Primary empirical source: release date/identifier, Household Survey Data headline targets, full Table A-1 TOTAL column header and selected levels/rates; archived technical-note definitions, reference period, seasonal adjustment, revisions and sampling/nonsampling limits. Supplies six actual historical aggregate records; chapter reconstruction and examples are original.
verification: Retrieved archived HTML through web retrieval and inspected release USDL-24-1571, 2 August 2024 08:30 EDT; narrative rate4.3, monthly +0.2 percentage point, unemployment +352,000 and July7.2million. Inspected all nine Table A-1 column labels and TOTAL population/labor-force/employed/unemployed/rate/not-in-labor-force rows before manually transcribing positions1,2,3,4,8,9 for July2023/June2024/July2024 NSA and SA. Inspected footnote1 (population not seasonally adjusted), annual population-control note, household definitions/reference week, seasonal-adjustment/revision and reliability discussion. Summary Table A corroborated SA values. Scope is these specified sections, not every figure or claim in the release. A separate direct curl download returned HTTP403; no raw HTML file or original-source-byte hash is claimed. Frozen files are clearly labeled local manual extracts. Survey microdata, weights, seasonal factors and standard errors were not reconstructed. All six rates and the three baseline targets reproduce at declared display precision; annual SA rounding-order departure and two -1-thousand component residuals are recorded rather than silently balanced. Government public-use basis separately sourced below.

title: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics — Current Population Survey concepts and definitions
use: Primary definitions of civilian noninstitutional population age16+, United States geography, labor force, unemployed including temporary-layoff search exception, unemployment-rate denominator, participation and seasonal adjustment. Supports interpreting counts as estimated persons rather than survey sample size or payroll jobs.
verification: Retrieved live official definitions and inspected civilian noninstitutional population/exclusions, geography50states and DC, employed/unemployed/labor-force criteria, unemployment-rate formula and seasonal-adjustment discussion. Definitions were cross-checked with the archived release's technical note. This is a live explanatory page inspected on the stated date, not a frozen copy asserted to be identical in2024, and not a claim to verify every labor-force definition or all methodological revisions.
